items.title: Local quasi-finiteness is a local property of ring maps and is characterized by it on affine charts
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent ways of saying that a morphism is locally quasi-finite, together with the stability of the property under restriction to open subschemes (statement lines 4055-4076). The counted proof is a reduction rather than a citation: it defines the ring-level property, verifies the three local-property conditions for it by appealing to the fact that quasi-finiteness at a prime depends only on the local ring and by arguing through a cover of the ring by localizations, and then invokes the local-property machinery and the pointwise characterization to conclude (proof lines 4078-4110). It is H2: the argument is a well-structured reduction carried out inside the counted span, with no independent research-level content.
